questions.qtext: Out of given alternatives, choose the one which best expresses the meaning of the word, Envoy
questions.solution:
(c)
The word “Envoy” refers to a person who is sent as a representative, often on a diplomatic
mission. An ambassador is a senior diplomat or envoy representing a country. So, “Ambassador”
best expresses the meaning of the word “Envoy”.

questions.qtext:
Choose the word opposite in meaning for the underlined word:
The hot summer afternoon made everyone feel languid and they sought refuge in the shade to escape the heat.
questions.solution:
(b)
The word “Languid” means lacking energy, weak, or slow-often due to fatigue, illness, or heat.
In the context of the sentence, the hot summer afternoon made everyone feel fired and drained.
Hence, “Energetic” is the opposite in the meaning to “languid”.

questions.qtext:
Select the part (option) of the below sentence that contains an error :
He was consulted seldom by his colleagues while making important decisions on financial matters.
questions.solution:
(a)
The adverb of frequency, “seldom,” should typically be placed before the main verb “consulted.”
Thus, the correct sentence is:
He was seldom consulted by his collegues while making important decisions on financial matters.

questions.qtext:
Select the alternative which is the best substitute of the sentence/word:
Take away or alter the natural qualities of
questions.solution:

Denature : Changed from its natural state.
Unadulterated : Pure, not mixed or diluted with any different or extra elements.

questions.qtext:
The World Health Organisation is briefly called W.H.O. It is a specialised agency of the United Nations and was established in 1948.  International health workers can be seen working in all kinds of surroundings: in deserts, jungles, mountains, coconut groves, and rice fields. They help the sick to attain health and the healthy to maintain their health. This global health team assists the local health workers in stopping the spread of what are called communicable diseases, like cholera. These diseases can spread from one country to another and so can be a threat to world health. W.H.O. assists different national health authorities not only in controlling diseases but also in preventing them altogether. Total prevention of diseases is possible in a number of ways. Everyone knows how people, particularly children, are vaccinated against one disease or another. Similarly, most people are familiar with the spraying of houses with poisonous substances which kill disease-carrying insects.
"It is a specialised agency of the United Nations and was established in 1948.” Here specialised means

options.text: made suitable for a particular purpose

questions.solution:
(d)
The word “specialised” refers to something that is focused on a specific area or purpose rather
than being general. In the sentence, W.H.O. is described as a specialised agency — meaning it is
an agency that deals specifically with health matters, not with everything else. Thus, “made
suitable for a particular purpose” is the most accurate meaning.
(A) expert: relates to skill, but “specialised” here talks about focus, not expertise.
(B) extraordinary: means very special or unusual — not the meaning here.
(C) uncommon: means rare — not the intended meaning.

questions.qtext:
In questions no. 12 and 13, one/two statements are given followed by two/three conclusions. You have to consider the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statements.

Statement:
Sun is the source of light.
Conclusions:
I. Moon is not the source of light
II. Light has only one source.
questions.solution:
(d)
The statement only mentions sun as a source of light but it does not deny other sources (like Moon,
bulbs, fire etc.) and it does not say sun is the only source. Therefore, both conclusions are wrong.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
Statement:
I. All cities are towns.
II. Some cities are villages.
Conclusions:
I. All villages are towns.
II. No village is a town.
III. Some villages are towns.
questions.solution:
(a)
Some cities are villages, and all cities are towns. So, those villages (which are cities) are also
towns. Hence, some villages are towns.
So, only conclusion III is correct.
